# ociext_nsg_peer_rules (Resource)

Security rules of an NSG whose source or destination is an NSG, including the NSG itself. They live apart from `ociext_nsg` so that NSGs can reference each other without a dependency cycle: Terraform creates the NSGs first and then their peer rules. The resource owns every rule of type NSG of the NSG: those rules created outside Terraform are removed on the next apply. Use only one per NSG. Creating it fails if the NSG already has rules of type NSG that are not in the configuration; import them instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Two NSGs that reference each other. With the rules inside ociext_nsg this
# would be a dependency cycle; here Terraform creates both NSGs first and then
# their peer rules.
resource "ociext_nsg" "app" {
  compartment_id = var.compartment_id
  vcn_id         = var.vcn_id
  display_name   = "nsg-app"

  rules = [
    { direction = "INGRESS", protocol = "tcp", source = "0.0.0.0/0", ports = "443" },
    { direction = "EGRESS", protocol = "all", destination = "0.0.0.0/0" },
  ]
}

resource "ociext_nsg" "db" {
  compartment_id = var.compartment_id
  vcn_id         = var.vcn_id
  display_name   = "nsg-db"
}

resource "ociext_nsg_peer_rules" "app" {
  nsg_id = ociext_nsg.app.id

  rules = [
    # Traffic between the instances of the app NSG itself.
    { direction = "INGRESS", protocol = "all", source = ociext_nsg.app.id },
    { direction = "EGRESS", protocol = "tcp", destination = ociext_nsg.db.id, ports = "5432" },
  ]
}

resource "ociext_nsg_peer_rules" "db" {
  nsg_id = ociext_nsg.db.id

  rules = [
    { direction = "INGRESS", protocol = "tcp", source = ociext_nsg.app.id, ports = "5432", description = "PostgreSQL from app" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `nsg_id` (String) OCID of the network security group the rules belong to.
- `rules` (Attributes Set) Security rules of the NSG whose source or destination is an NSG. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) OCID of the network security group, the same as `nsg_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `direction` (String) `INGRESS` or `EGRESS`.
- `protocol` (String) `all`, a protocol name or an IANA protocol number between 1 and 254. Names: `icmp` (1), `ipip` (4), `tcp` (6), `udp` (17), `gre` (47), `esp` (50), `ah` (51), `icmpv6` (58), `ospf` (89), `vrrp` (112), `sctp` (132). Ports are only allowed with `tcp` and `udp`, and ICMP type and code with `icmp` and `icmpv6`. A rule keeps the spelling used in the configuration, so `gre` and `47` are the same rule.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Description. Changing it updates the rule in place.
- `destination` (String) Required for `EGRESS`. Same formats as `source`.
- `icmp_code` (Number) ICMP code. Needs `icmp_type`; all codes when not set.
- `icmp_type` (Number) ICMP type. Only for `icmp` and `icmpv6`; all types when not set.
- `ports` (String) Destination port (`443`) or range (`8000-8100`). Only for `tcp` and `udp`; all ports when not set.
- `source` (String) Required for `INGRESS`. OCID of an NSG. It can be the NSG of `nsg_id` itself.
- `source_ports` (String) Source port or range. Only for `tcp` and `udp`; all ports when not set.
- `stateless` (Boolean) Whether the rule is stateless. Defaults to `false`. Changing it updates the rule in place.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imports all the rules of type NSG of an NSG, by the NSG OCID.
terraform import ociext_nsg_peer_rules.app ocid1.networksecuritygroup.oc1.eu-frankfurt-1.aaaa...
```
